raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 26 years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil. Quzhou County winters are cold and dry, summers get hot. My 5 mu isn't big, but it's mine. My wife's brother works in Shijiazhuang now, sends money back sometimes — that helps — but I still need the fields to produce.

I grow spring maize as my main crop. That's what sp.maize means for me — I plant after the last frost in late April, harvest in September. I'll put about 3.5 mu into maize. For seeds, I buy hybrid seeds from the county agricultural supply store. I started doing that maybe 15 years ago when yields jumped. I'm not going back to traditional seed. My neighbor still uses saved seed — his yields are lower every year.

For the kidney beans, I plant on the remaining 1.5 mu, a bit later in May. I use improved variety seeds — not hybrid, those are expensive for beans and I'm not sure the premium is worth it on beans. Beans help rest that section of soil a little too.

Fertilizer — I apply what my father taught me adjusted for what I've seen work. For maize I put down base fertilizer when I till, then top-dress nitrogen when the crop is knee high. I have well water so I can irrigate when the plants need it. I'll irrigate the maize about 4 times — seeding, jointing, tasseling, and grain filling. Beans get 2-3 times. I use rotary tillage — I rent the tractor from the village cooperative.

Pesticides — I spray when I see pests or disease, typically 2 times on maize, once on beans. I don't spray on a schedule, I watch the crop.
